assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, via Katori's magic-wavelength proposal and Ye's Sr clocks, reached fractional uncertainties near 1e-18 and now outperform the caesium definition of the second. They link atomic structure, laser cooling and frequency-comb metrology, and they enable relativistic geodesy and fundamental-constant searches. The concept is clear and the impact is lasting.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice and led early Sr work. Ye's group drove the record accuracy and the clock-comparison programme. Two laureates fit cleanly. Others (e.g. Ludlow, Derevianko theory, Takamoto) are not in the credited list and cannot be added.
assessment.maturity: Independent confirmation across several international laboratories is excellent and the technology is about two decades old. Recognition is timely. The redefinition of the second is still in progress, which does not weaken the science.
uncertainties: Whether the committee wants to separate the lattice-clock concept from the later ion and Al+ clock lines, which are not credited here.
Relative weight of Katori's proposal versus Ye's accuracy milestones is a judgment call.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theoretical prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and the Z2 topological classification opened a new class of quantum matter. The HgTe/CdTe experiment confirmed edge-state transport. The field is conceptually deep, widely influential, and connects to spin-orbit physics I know well from relativistic atomic structure.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the decisive theoretical step (Z2 invariant, quantum spin Hall in graphene). Molenkamp's group delivered the first experimental realisation, together with the Zhang-Bernevig-Hughes prediction, which is not credited here. M. Zahid Hasan led the 3D topological insulator observations but must be left out of a three-person prize. A fair trio is possible but contentious.
assessment.maturity: Predictions from 2005-2006 were confirmed by many independent groups, including 3D materials. Interpretation is stable and recognition is more than timely.
uncertainties: Omission of Bernevig, Zhang and Hughes (not credited) and of the 3D topological-insulator experimenters creates an allocation dispute.
Choice between Molenkamp and Hasan for the experimental slot is not settled by the supplied credit.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BB84 and the entanglement-based E91 protocol founded quantum cryptography, whose security rests on quantum mechanics. The ideas are original, simple, and have driven a large experimental and commercial field and the foundations of quantum information.
assessment.attribution: Bennett and Brassard introduced BB84; Ekert introduced the entanglement-based protocol linked to Bell tests. The three names give a coherent configuration. Wiesner's earlier conjugate-coding idea, not credited here, is a credit complication.
assessment.maturity: Protocols have been demonstrated over fibre and satellite links by many groups. Practical security loopholes are still being addressed, but the theoretical content is stable. Recognition is overdue rather than premature.
uncertainties: Attribution of priority to Wiesner and others is not resolved by the supplied credit.
Debate over whether a fundamental-physics prize is the right home for a protocol invention.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The Cirac-Zoller proposal for quantum gates with trapped ions and the related ideas for atomic quantum simulation set out how to compute and simulate with controlled atoms. As an atomic theorist I regard this as a clear case of theory shaping experiment across AMO physics. The impact on ion and neutral-atom platforms is lasting.
assessment.attribution: The pair are the clear originators of the 1995 gate proposal and the joint theory programme. The credited names fit a two-person prize without ambiguity. Experimental realisations by others (Wineland group, Blatt, Monroe) are not credited here.
assessment.maturity: Experimental realisation has been repeated by many ion groups and the field is advancing to larger processors. The 2012 prize recognised ion control, so the theoretical founding contribution is a natural follow-on. Timing is good.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2012 prize and with possible experimental quantum-computing recognition (not credited here).
Cirac and Zoller also appear in the broader optical-lattice candidate; this entry should not double count.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of flat bands at a magic angle and the discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in twisted bilayer graphene created the moire-materials field. The finding was unexpected, and the platform is a highly tunable testbed for strongly correlated matter.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the theoretical prediction and Jarillo-Herrero led the experimental discovery, with the first author Cao as a student. The trio is natural, though the supplied credit omits Cao and other contributors.
assessment.maturity: Replicated widely and extended to many moire systems. Origin of superconductivity and the correlated phases is still debated, so the interpretation is not fully settled. Recognition is early but defensible.
uncertainties: Possible competing credit (e.g. Dos Santos, Peres, Castro Neto, Suarez Morell) is not in the supplied list.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: IceCube opened neutrino astronomy by detecting a diffuse astrophysical neutrino flux and linking a neutrino to the blazar TXS 0506+056 and to the Galactic plane. It is a large instrument-driven discovery and a new observational window.
assessment.attribution: Halzen is the central intellectual leader of IceCube. Karle and Spiering were important in the AMANDA-to-IceCube development, but credit within a very large collaboration is hard to narrow to three names.
assessment.maturity: Diffuse-flux detection is robust and the source associations are growing, although individual source identification is still limited. The field is clearly maturing; outside my own expertise.
uncertainties: Fairness of a three-person subset of a collaboration of hundreds.
Source identification is not fully mature and the supplied credit does not include earlier detector pioneers.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED brought strong light-matter coupling to superconducting circuits and underlies superconducting quantum processors. The concept is a clean analogue of cavity QED and has had major impact on quantum control and readout.
assessment.attribution: Blais and colleagues proposed the architecture, while Wallraff and Schoelkopf demonstrated strong coupling in 2004. The three-person split is plausible; Girvin and Devoret (the latter a 2025 laureate) are not credited here.
assessment.maturity: Widely reproduced. The 2025 prize recognised closely related superconducting-circuit macroscopic quantum tunnelling, so a second prize in this area may be seen as premature. I also note no direct involvement of mine in this field.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2025 prize may make a further award in the same area unwelcome.
Credit of the underlying idea versus the first demonstration is not unique.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Aberration-corrected electron microscopy broke the spherical-aberration limit and gave sub-angstrom imaging of atoms in materials. It is an instrumentation advance with a precedent in the 1986 prize, and it has broad impact on materials physics and condensed matter.
assessment.attribution: Rose proposed the correctors, Haider and Urban built the first working correctors and applied them. The three names match a clean split of theory, construction and application. Others, such as Krivanek, are not credited here.
assessment.maturity: Independently confirmed and commercially standard for two decades. Recognition is timely or overdue. The advance is instrument-focused, which weighs against a physics emphasis.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views instrumentation of this kind as sufficiently physics-oriented.
Priority claims of other corrector groups are not resolved in the supplied credit.
